blocks.correctApproach: Emit from the parent's own components, or have the table emit `update:row`. Keep slot props read-only in the contract.

blocks.title: Production guidance
blocks.content: Type the slot, key the list in the owner, and keep slot props small.
keyPoints: Use `defineSlots` when more than one slot exists or the props are easy to mix up.
Provide fallback content for the default rendering.
Check `useSlots()` only when the layout truly depends on whether a slot was passed.
Do not reach into child instance state from slot content.

blocks.title: Quick revision and official references
blocks.content:
Quick revision

- The parent compiles slot content in the parent scope.
- Child data reaches that content only as slot props.
- Fallback markup renders when the parent omits the slot.
- Scoped slots replace boolean prop explosions when layout is open-ended.

Official references

- https://vuejs.org/guide/components/slots.html

title: provide and inject
description: Ancestor-to-descendant dependencies, app-level providers, and the reactivity rules.

blocks.title: Provide is an explicit implicit dependency
blocks.content:
`provide` makes a value available to descendants without threading it through every prop. `inject` reads the nearest provider. It is the right tool for a theme, a form root, or a tree-scoped store that many distant nodes need. It is the wrong tool for a value only the direct child needs. That value should stay a prop so the dependency is visible in the template.

Use a `InjectionKey<T>` symbol, not a string, when TypeScript should know the injected type. Strings collide across libraries. Provide the key from a composable such as `provideForm(form)` so callers do not sprinkle raw `provide` calls with slightly different shapes.
keyPoints: The nearest ancestor provider wins. An intermediate component can override.
`app.provide` covers every component in that app instance.
The default argument to `inject` is used when nobody provided the key.
Plugins and libraries should provide symbols, not mutate `globalProperties`, for new code.

blocks.title: Provide the reactive source, not a snapshot
blocks.content:
If you `provide` a plain number, descendants keep that number. If you provide a `ref` or a `reactive` object, descendants that use it stay connected, because they hold the same container. Destructuring a provided reactive object in the descendant copies values and drops tracking, just like any other reactive object.

Do not provide a computed's unwrapped result from a non-reactive snapshot taken once in setup. Provide the computed ref itself. And do not use provide/inject to sneak a mutation past a parent. The provider still owns the state and should expose functions for the changes descendants are allowed to make.
keyPoints: Provide refs or reactive objects when updates must flow.
Providing `count.value` provides a number, once.
Descendants should call functions the provider supplied (`setPage`, `registerField`) instead of mutating internal fields.
Injection makes unit tests responsible for supplying a provider or a default.

blocks.title: A typed form context
blocks.explanation: Descendants call `useFormContext()` and receive the same reactive object. The symbol key prevents a string clash with another library's `form` provider.

blocks.title: Interview question
blocks.question: How do you choose between props, provide/inject, and a Pinia store?
blocks.answer:
Props are the default for a parent and child. Provide/inject fits a subtree that shares context, such as a form, a tabs root, or a theme, where drilling would cross components that do not care. Pinia fits state that many unrelated routes share, that must outlive one component tree, or that you want to inspect in devtools as an application store.

I would not put a page's temporary hover state in Pinia, and I would not provide the entire store from the root when only one subtree needs a scoped override. Provide/inject can override per subtree. A singleton store cannot, unless you design ids into it.
blocks.explanation: The lifetime and the audience of the state decide the channel.

blocks.title: A provided number never updates
blocks.question: A parent does `const count = ref(0)` and `provide("count", count.value)`. The child injects `count` and displays it. After the parent increments the ref, the child stays at 0. Why?
blocks.answer: The parent provided the current number, not the ref. Injection received a plain value with no connection to later assignments. Provide the ref itself (`provide(key, count)`) and read `count.value` in the child, or provide a computed ref.
blocks.explanation:
Provide does not make an arbitrary value reactive. It passes the value you handed it.

[Further reading](https://vuejs.org/guide/components/provide-inject.html)
hints: What JavaScript value was passed into `provide`?

blocks.title: Senior scenario
blocks.question: A design system has nested menus. Inner items need to close the root menu, and a second menu on the page must not close the first. How do you model that?
blocks.answer:
The root menu provides a context object with `close()` and a generated id. Items inject the nearest context, so an inner menu that provides its own context handles its own children. The page does not use a global store for "the open menu", because two menus would fight.

Keyboard handling and focus restoration live on the root that provided the context. Items call `close()` rather than reaching into the root's refs.
blocks.explanation: Nearest-provider injection matches nested widgets better than a singleton.

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.mistake: Using string keys such as `provide("theme", theme)` inside a shared component library.
blocks.whyItHappens: Strings are easy to type. Another package provides the same string and one tree silently receives the wrong object.
blocks.correctApproach: Export an `InjectionKey` symbol from the library and a `useTheme()` that throws or returns a documented default when the provider is missing.

blocks.title: Production guidance
blocks.content: Provide the smallest context object, with functions for the allowed writes.
keyPoints: Prefer props when the consumer is a direct child.
Provide refs, not `.value` snapshots, when the UI must update.
Type the key with `InjectionKey`.
In tests, mount with a provider or cover the missing-provider path.

blocks.title: Quick revision and official references
blocks.content:
Quick revision

- `inject` reads the nearest `provide` or an app-level provider.
- Providing `.value` snapshots a plain JavaScript value.
- Symbol keys beat string keys in libraries.
- Use provide for subtree context, props for local input, Pinia for app lifetime.

Official references

- https://vuejs.org/guide/components/provide-inject.html

title: Fallthrough attributes
description: How undeclared attributes land on the root node, and how to retarget them.

blocks.title: Attrs are everything you did not declare
blocks.content:
If a parent passes `class`, `style`, `id`, `data-*`, or a native listener that the child did not declare as a prop or emit, Vue treats it as a fallthrough attribute. A single-root component applies those attributes to its root element automatically. Declared props and declared emits are removed from that set, which is why `@saved` does not become a DOM `saved` listener after you declare it.

`class` and `style` are special: they merge with the child root's own class and style instead of replacing them. Other attributes overwrite when the child also sets the same name on the root.
keyPoints: Fallthrough applies to a single root. Multi-root components do not auto-apply attrs, and Vue warns.
`inheritAttrs: false` turns off automatic application. You then place them yourself.
`useAttrs()` reads the fallthrough object in `<script setup>`.
Listeners in attrs are not component emits. Declare emits you consider part of the API.

blocks.title: Wrappers must choose which inner node receives the attrs
blocks.content:
A text-field component whose root is a `<label>` should not dump `placeholder` and `@focus` onto the label. Set `defineOptions({ inheritAttrs: false })` and put `v-bind="attrs"` on the `<input>`. Merge `class` deliberately if both the wrapper and the input need classes.

Attrs are not a second props system. Anything the component wants to document, default, or validate should be a prop. Leaving `disabled` as an accidental fallthrough attr hides it from TypeScript and from the emits/props contract.
keyPoints: Retarget attrs in wrapper components.
Do not forward attrs to multiple nodes unless you split them on purpose.
Declare real API as props and emits so they leave the attrs object.
In a multi-root component, forwarding is mandatory if the parent is allowed to pass attributes.

blocks.title: Forward attrs to the inner input
blocks.code:
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useAttrs } from 'vue'

defineOptions({ inheritAttrs: false })
defineProps<{ label: string }>()
const attrs = useAttrs()
</script>

<template>
  <label class="field">
    {{ label }}
    <input v-bind="attrs" />
  </label>
</template>
blocks.explanation: `label` is a prop, so it is not forwarded. `placeholder`, `class`, and native listeners from the parent land on the input because that is the node with `v-bind="attrs"`.

blocks.title: Interview question
blocks.question: A parent sets `disabled` on your component and nothing happens. Where do you look?
blocks.answer:
I check whether `disabled` was declared as a prop. If it was not, it fallthroughs to the root node. If the root is a `<div>` and the real control is inside, the attribute never reaches the control. The fix is either to declare `disabled` as a prop and bind it to the control, or to set `inheritAttrs: false` and forward attrs to the control.

I also check for a fragment root. Automatic fallthrough does not pick a node for you in that case.
blocks.explanation: Fallthrough goes to the root element only. Wrapper components have to aim it.

blocks.title: The listener that became a DOM listener
blocks.question: A parent writes `@select="onSelect"` on a card component, and a native `select` event fires from an inner control at the wrong time. The child never declared `select` in `defineEmits`. What happened?
blocks.answer: Undeclared listeners fall through toward the root element as native listeners. `select` can be a DOM event, so the parent listener is attached to the DOM rather than treated as a component emit. Declare `select` in `defineEmits` if it is a component event. If it was meant for the inner control, forward attrs onto that control on purpose.
blocks.explanation:
Declaring the emit removes it from fallthrough attrs and makes it part of the component contract.

[Further reading](https://vuejs.org/guide/components/attrs.html)
hints: What does Vue do with a listener that is not a declared emit?

blocks.title: Senior scenario
blocks.question: You are building a design-system button that renders either `<button>` or `<a>` based on an `href` prop. Parents must be able to pass `class`, `aria-*`, and click handlers once. How do you forward them?
blocks.answer:
Declare the props you interpret (`href`, `variant`, `disabled`). Turn off automatic inheritance and bind the remaining attrs onto the actual `<button>` or `<a>`, not onto a wrapper span. Map `disabled` yourself because an anchor does not support it the same way: use `aria-disabled` and ignore the click when the link variant is disabled.

Add tests for both roots. Class merge is easy to get wrong when the component also sets a variant class.
blocks.explanation: The attribute target is the node the user activates, and it changes with the variant.

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.mistake: Binding `v-bind="$attrs"` and also leaving `inheritAttrs` at its default `true`.
blocks.whyItHappens: Attributes are applied twice: once by fallthrough on the root and once by the explicit bind, so listeners fire twice.
blocks.correctApproach: Set `inheritAttrs: false` before you place attrs yourself.

blocks.title: Production guidance
blocks.content: Document the attribute target of every wrapper component.
keyPoints: Declare props and emits that are part of the API.
Forward the rest to one inner node in wrappers.
Disable automatic inheritance when you forward manually.
Treat multi-root components as manual-forwarding components.

blocks.title: Quick revision and official references
blocks.content:
Quick revision

- Undeclared attributes fall through to a single root.
- Class and style merge. Other names can overwrite.
- Wrappers set `inheritAttrs: false` and bind attrs to the inner control.
- Declared emits stop being native fallthrough listeners.

Official references

- https://vuejs.org/guide/components/attrs.html
